`::before` and `::after` refer to CSS pseudo-elements that are created before and after matching elements.
Pseudo-elements are typically not shown in HTML element trees.
However, if you are using the right kind of a debugging tool (like Chrome inspector) you can see these special elements.
As its nowadays very common to style a page using pseudo-selectors, it is very useful to have a debugging tool that can display them.
Sign up to request clarification or add additional context in comments.
If Chrome is displaying those pseudo-elements in the inspector then presumably some content is already being added to them.
But `::before` and `::after` are not displayed in the actual page.
Also, I'm referring to HTML element structure, not the actual view of the page, but I can see I wasn't exactly enough with that!
